issues.detail: The Hebrew 'רַב מְחוֹלֵל כֹּל' means 'one who hires a fool is like one who hires passersby' — the subject is 'one who hires' (שׂוֹכֵר), not 'a wise/skillful person' (Người khôn khéo). The Vietnamese adds 'Người khôn khéo' (a wise/skillful person) which is not in the Hebrew, and mistranslates 'מְחוֹלֵל' (causes/incites) as 'khiến cho mọi người đều sai lầm' (causes everyone to err), whereas the Hebrew says 'one who hires a fool' (שׂוֹכֵר כְּסִיל) — the first clause is about hiring a fool, not causing error. The verse's claim is altered: the Hebrew contrasts hiring a fool with hiring passersby, but the Vietnamese introduces a different subject and action.
